about: Test vectors of canvas's crop for checking, R25 in docs/decisions.md: from the strokes a sheet shows and their groups (R24; vectors/groups.json) to the crop's numbers at each height of digits — the median, the height the digits are drawn at, the scale, the line, the size, the margins, where the crop lies on the sheet and the frames of the groups. Not its pixels: two implementations may draw them a level of grey apart. A proposal for the eval protocol, epic E3 in spec's RUN.md: the protocol's own vectors come in spec's releases, and canvas will test against those.

formulas.tenths: every place is taken in whole tenths of a unit, t(v) = round(10 × v), half up: 100.05 units are 1001 tenths (R24). B is the box of all the points, in tenths
formulas.bundles: the strokes whose points span flat × 10 tenths or more from top to bottom, joined by a chain of boxes that touch or overlap, 0 tenths apart or less both across and down; a lower stroke is a line and joins nothing
formulas.median: m, the lower median of the heights of the bundles, the ⌊(n − 1) / 2⌋-th from the lowest, in tenths, or flat × 10 if there is no bundle; the scale takes H = min(m, ceiling × 10). The case's median is m / 10 units
formulas.size: for D′ from the digit asked for down to 1: w₀ = ⌈(B.xmax − B.xmin) × D′ / H⌉ + 2 × margin and h₀ = ⌈(B.ymax − B.ymin) × D′ / H⌉ + 2 × margin; width = max(w₀, side), left = margin + ⌊(width − w₀) / 2⌋, and height and top alike. D′ is drawn, the first for which max(width, height) ≤ edge and ⌈width / patch⌉ × ⌈height / patch⌉ ≤ tokens
formulas.scale: 10 × D′ / H px to a unit; the line is max(D′, 12) / 12 px wide
formulas.sheetBox: [(B.ymin × D′ − top × H) / (10 × D′), (B.xmin × D′ − left × H) / (10 × D′), (B.ymin × D′ − top × H + height × H) / (10 × D′), (B.xmin × D′ − left × H + width × H) / (10 × D′)] units: each one division of two whole numbers
formulas.frames: for each group, g the box of its points in tenths, r = (max(D′, 12) + 24) × H, X(x) = 24 × ((x − B.xmin) × D′ + left × H) and Y(y) = 24 × ((y − B.ymin) × D′ + top × H): [⌊1000 × (Y(g.ymin) − r) / (24 × H × height)⌋, ⌊1000 × (X(g.xmin) − r) / (24 × H × width)⌋, ⌈1000 × (Y(g.ymax) + r) / (24 × H × height)⌉, ⌈1000 × (X(g.xmax) + r) / (24 × H × width)⌉] — the group's ink, its points widened by half the line and the pixel at its edge, rounded outward: every pixel the ink touches lies within, and min < max
formulas.numbers: every whole number above stays below 2^53, so a double holds it exactly, and an int64 does too; the numbers that are not whole are each one division of two whole numbers

cases.name: staircase
cases.about: The research's example: a ladder of two posts and seven rungs, «30» beside it after a pause, «180 : 30 = 5» after another, the 5 erased, then 6, ringed.

cases.name: later
cases.about: «12 + 5 =», and 8 s later «17» right after it: what is written later next to old writing is a group of its own (R06).

cases.name: lines
cases.about: Two lines a cell apart, the second begun 1.5 s after the first, with no pause to think: a group each.

cases.name: signs
cases.about: 3/4 + 1/4 = 1 in fractions over bars, underlined; 3 s later «12 : 4 = 3» below: a group each, with their bars, dots and lines.

cases.name: words
cases.about: Two lines of joined-up words, each word a stroke, with the dot of an i put after its word: a group a line.

cases.name: tutor
cases.about: Two lines as tutor's synthetic writer draws them: digits 36 high, 26 apart, lines 80 apart, 1.5 s before a line and 120 to 249 ms between strokes.

cases.name: crossed
cases.about: A line crossed out at once, 0.4 s after it, which is of its group; another crossed out 3 s after it, which is a group of its own.

cases.name: bridge
cases.about: «12» and «34» far apart, a line under both 0.3 s on, which joins them; «56» and «78» the same, the line 4 s on, which joins neither.

cases.name: undone
cases.about: «12» erased and brought back by undo 3 s on, «3» written next to it 0.5 s after that, the sheet cleared and that undone: «12» keeps the time it was written, a group apart from «3».

cases.name: bounds
cases.about: Pairs at the rule's bounds and just past them: 2000 and 2001 ms, 50 and 50.1 units across, 50 and 50.1 down.

cases.name: rounding
cases.about: Dots in hundredths of a unit and fractions of a millisecond, in pairs. The rule rounds half up: 100.05 units are 1001 tenths, so the first pair is 500 tenths apart across, the fourth 2000 ms apart and the sixth 500 tenths apart down — neighbours all three, which rounding half to even or cutting the fraction off would part. The second pair, 50.02 units apart, is 501 tenths, and the third and fifth come out at the bounds from just above.

cases.name: ladder
cases.about: A ladder alone, two posts 300 high and seven rungs. The rungs are lines, the posts two bundles, and their median, 300, is over the ceiling: the scale takes 100, and the ladder comes out three digits high.

cases.name: ladder-30
cases.about: The ladder and «30» beside it: four bundles, the two posts and the two digits, and the lower median of them is a digit's height.

cases.name: house
cases.about: A house — walls, a roof of two strokes, a door and a window, all touching — and «3» beside it: the house is one bundle 300 high, the digit another, and the lower median of the two is the digit.

cases.name: fraction
cases.about: «3/4 = 6/8», each bar touching both its digits, which are 2 units apart: the bars are lines and join nothing, so each digit is a bundle of its own.

cases.name: rows
cases.about: Three rows of digits 50 high, a row to a cell of the default grid, each touching the next: the digits of a column join into one bundle 150 high, and the median is over the ceiling. The rule's weak spot, and one reason for its ceiling.

cases.name: slant
cases.about: «5» and an underline 150 long that slants 4°, 10.5 units from end to end: under the floor of 15, a line, so the median is the digit's.

cases.name: ringed
cases.about: «7 − 1 = 6» with a ring round the 6: the ring's box holds the digit's, so the two are one bundle 56 high, and the lower median of the three bundles is a digit's.

cases.name: crossed-out
cases.about: «47 + 19 = 56» crossed out by an X over the whole line, and «47 + 19 = 66» written below: the X joins the line it crosses into one bundle 46 high, and the line below gives the median.

cases.name: table
cases.about: A drawn table of two rows and two columns, a number in each cell clear of its lines: the upright lines are bundles 120 high, the others are lines, and the digits give the median.

cases.name: column
cases.about: 47 + 19 summed in a column without a pause to think: one group 141 high, but each digit a bundle of its own, so the median is a digit's.

cases.name: fours
cases.about: «4 + 4 = 8»: each 4, of two strokes that cross, is one bundle, the + a bundle 21.6 high, and the lower median of the four is a digit's.

cases.name: dashes
cases.about: Three minus signs and a dot: lines, all of them, so there is no bundle and the median is the floor, 15.

cases.name: dot
cases.about: A dot alone: no bundle, so the median is the floor, and the crop is 200 px each way, the least, the dot in its middle.

cases.name: whole
cases.about: Digits at the top left corner, in the middle and at the bottom right corner: the work is the whole sheet. Its crop fits Claude's standard tier at 32 px, and at 48 px it would not, so its digits come out 32 px.

cases.name: answer
cases.about: A one-digit answer, under the least size of a crop: the crop is 200 px each way, and its margins widen to keep the digit in the middle.

cases.name: touching
cases.about: Two strokes 36 high whose boxes touch at a corner, 0 tenths apart: one bundle 72 high.

cases.name: apart
cases.about: The same strokes, the second a tenth of a unit to the right: two bundles 36 high.

cases.name: under-floor
cases.about: A stroke 36 high and one 14.9 high, 149 tenths: a line, so the median is the first's.

cases.name: at-floor
cases.about: A stroke 36 high and one 15 high, 150 tenths: at the floor a bundle, and the lower median of the two is 15.

cases.name: under-ceiling
cases.about: One stroke 99.9 high, 999 tenths: the scale takes it as it is.

cases.name: at-ceiling
cases.about: One stroke 100 high, 1000 tenths: the ceiling itself.

cases.name: over-ceiling
cases.about: One stroke 100.1 high, 1001 tenths: the scale takes 100.

cases.name: limit
cases.about: Three dots that span 660 by 1362 units: no bundle, so the median is 15. At 17 px the crop is 772 by 1568 px, 28 by 56 tiles of 28 px, 1568 tokens: at both of Claude's limits at once. From 18 px up it is drawn at 17.
